{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb",
      "line": 72,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Translation cache key ignores dynamic fallback chain",
      "body": "The LRU cache key only contains the translation key, current locale, and backend object id. This PR makes fallback resolution depend on SiteSetting.default_locale (and always :en). If two requests use the same I18n.locale but have different default locales (for example in multisite, or after an admin changes default_locale without a full I18n cache clear), a fallback translation cached for one context can be returned for another, serving the wrong language until the cache is cleared or evicted. Include the fallback chain/default locale/site identifier in the cache key, or invalidate this cache when fallback inputs change."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/application_controller.rb",
      "line": 159,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Fallback locales are only ensured loaded for controller requests",
      "body": "I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale. The translate accelerator lazily loads only the current locale inside I18n.translate, so fallback target locales (site default and :en) are not loaded in mailers, Sidekiq jobs, rake tasks, console, middleware, or any code path that translates without passing through this controller filter. In those contexts, missing translations will not fall back and may return translation-missing strings or raise instead. Fallback locales should be ensured whenever I18n.locale is set or inside the translate path."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb",
      "line": 68,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "translate still assumes @loaded_locales is initialized",
      "body": "The new ensure_loaded! method initializes @loaded_locales, but translate still calls @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale) without initializing it. If any code calls I18n.translate before ensure_loaded!, reload!, or load_locale has run, this will raise NoMethodError on nil. translate should use a memoized/synchronized accessor or initialize @loaded_locales before checking it."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb",
      "line": 63,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Locale-loaded flag initialization is not synchronized",
      "body": "@loaded_locales ||= [] in ensure_loaded! happens outside LOAD_MUTEX. On first concurrent use, multiple threads can race on assignment; one thread can overwrite the array after another has recorded loaded locales, causing duplicate locale loading or transient inconsistent state. Initialization and checks of @loaded_locales should be done under LOAD_MUTEX or through a synchronized memoized accessor."
    },
    {
      "file": "config/initializers/i18n.rb",
      "line": 24,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests for new fallback/loading behavior",
      "body": "This PR changes global I18n fallback order, lazy locale loading, and request-time loading, but adds no specs covering: missing translations falling back to SiteSetting.default_locale and :en; loading of fallback locales outside controllers; or cache invalidation when default_locale changes. Without tests, regressions in fallback behavior or cache staleness are likely."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores dynamic fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU cache key only contains the translation key, current locale, and backend object id. This PR makes fallback resolution depend on SiteSetting.default_locale (and always :en). If two requests use the same I18n.locale but have different default locales (for example in multisite, or after an admin changes default_locale without a full I18n cache clear), a fallback translation cached for one context can be returned for another, serving the wrong language until the cache is cleared or evicted. Include the fallback chain/default locale/site identifier in the cache key, or invalidate this cache when fallback inputs change.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only ensured loaded for controller requests
findings.body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale. The translate accelerator lazily loads only the current locale inside I18n.translate, so fallback target locales (site default and :en) are not loaded in mailers, Sidekiq jobs, rake tasks, console, middleware, or any code path that translates without passing through this controller filter. In those contexts, missing translations will not fall back and may return translation-missing strings or raise instead. Fallback locales should be ensured whenever I18n.locale is set or inside the translate path.

findings.title: translate still assumes @loaded_locales is initialized
findings.body: The new ensure_loaded! method initializes @loaded_locales, but translate still calls @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale) without initializing it. If any code calls I18n.translate before ensure_loaded!, reload!, or load_locale has run, this will raise NoMethodError on nil. translate should use a memoized/synchronized accessor or initialize @loaded_locales before checking it.

findings.title: Locale-loaded flag initialization is not synchronized
findings.body: @loaded_locales ||= [] in ensure_loaded! happens outside LOAD_MUTEX. On first concurrent use, multiple threads can race on assignment; one thread can overwrite the array after another has recorded loaded locales, causing duplicate locale loading or transient inconsistent state. Initialization and checks of @loaded_locales should be done under LOAD_MUTEX or through a synchronized memoized accessor.

findings.title: No tests for new fallback/loading behavior
findings.body: This PR changes global I18n fallback order, lazy locale loading, and request-time loading, but adds no specs covering: missing translations falling back to SiteSetting.default_locale and :en; loading of fallback locales outside controllers; or cache invalidation when default_locale changes. Without tests, regressions in fallback behavior or cache staleness are likely.
